2026-11-28|ls-crz: CRZ rules: how far from the coast you can build Land School · source: “CRZ Rules in India: How Far From the Coast You Can Build” by 1acre.in Key Highlights CRZ rules control construction near the coastline — they decide whether a coastal plot is buildable at all. Four zones: CRZ-I (ecologically sensitive — essentially no building), II (urban coast), III (rural coast), IV (the water itself). The 2019 notification cut the rural No Development Zone from 200 m to 50 m in dense villages — but ONLY once the state’s Coastal Zone Management Plan is approved under it; until then 200 m continues. Every coastal project needs PRIOR clearance — courts have ordered completed buildings demolished for lacking it. Distance is measured from the officially demarcated High Tide Line, not the visible waterline. What the CRZ is and why it exists The Coastal Regulation Zone is the legal strip along India’s coastline within which activity is controlled — notified under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, with the central environment ministry as nodal authority and state Coastal Zone Management Authorities enforcing. The balance it strikes: protecting mangroves, wetlands and dunes, protecting fishing communities’ livelihoods, and still allowing coastal development — by classifying the coast into zones, each with its own rules on construction, industry and land conversion near the high tide line. Definition — High Tide Line (HTL): the officially DEMARCATED line the sea reaches at highest tide — mapped by authorised agencies, not eyeballed from the beach. Every setback measures from this line; measuring from the visible waterline is the classic buyer error. The four zones CRZ-I — ecologically sensitive: IA covers mangroves and coral reefs, IB the intertidal strip between tide lines; new construction essentially off the table, narrow exceptions for defence, atomic energy and major public infrastructure. CRZ-II — urban coast: already-developed municipal coastline; building allowed only LANDWARD of existing roads or authorised structures — never toward the sea — following local FSI/FAR. CRZ-III — rural coast, split by density (Census 2011): IIIA is dense rural coast (>2,161 people/sq km) with a 50-metre No Development Zone; IIIB is sparse coast at 200 metres. CRZ-IV — the water: IVA open sea from low tide line to 12 nautical miles, IVB tidal inland waters; traditional fishing protected, untreated discharge banned. Definition — No Development Zone (NDZ): the strip inland from the HTL where new construction is barred regardless of ownership. Owning land inside the NDZ means owning a view, not a building site. Zones at a glance Zone What it covers Building position CRZ-IA / IB Mangroves, reefs / intertidal strip Essentially none (defence & major public works excepted) CRZ-II Developed urban coast Landward of existing road/structure line only; local FSI applies CRZ-IIIA Dense rural coast (>2,161/km²) Beyond 50 m NDZ — once the state’s CZMP is approved; 200 m until then CRZ-IIIB Sparse rural coast Beyond 200 m NDZ CRZ-IVA / IVB Sea to 12 nm / tidal inland waters No construction; fishing protected, discharge banned What changed in 2019 Three big moves. The long-standing FREEZE on Floor Space Index in eligible coastal areas was lifted — development can follow local planning regulations, subject to CRZ conditions. Clearances were DECENTRALISED — state authorities now handle much more, with the centre appraising specified categories. And the rural NDZ was cut for dense villages — but here is the catch buyers miss: the relaxations take effect only after the state’s Coastal Zone Management Plan prepared under the 2019 framework is formally approved. Until that approval, the OLD setbacks continue. A “50-metre plot” in a state with an unapproved CZMP is still a 200-metre plot. Definition — Coastal Zone Management Plan (CZMP): the state’s official map of its coast — which stretch is which zone, where the HTL runs. The 2019 relaxations are switched on, state by state, only by its approval. What is permanently off-limits Whatever the zone: new industries, hazardous-substance storage, sand and coral mining, land reclamation and bunding within the regulated distance. Groundwater: no extraction within 200 m of the HTL except community use; between 200 and 500 m, only manual drawing from ordinary wells, and only where no alternative exists. Getting clearance Mandatory BEFORE any construction in the zone. Jurisdiction splits by category: CRZ-I and IV go to the central ministry; CRZ-II and III — covering most residential and commercial work — to the State CZMA. Small mercy for individuals: self-dwelling units up to 300 sq m get a simpler path through the local authority. Building without clearance is the one shortcut with a documented ending: courts have ordered COMPLETED buildings demolished. Example: A buyer takes a “beach-view villa plot” 120 m from the water in a dense fishing village, told “the new rules allow 50 m”. The state’s CZMP is still pending approval — so the 200 m NDZ applies, and the plot cannot host a villa at all. The seller quoted the notification; the buyer needed the CZMP status. Before you buy or build near the coast ☐ Confirm which CRZ regime applies to the EXACT survey number. ☐ Check whether the state’s CZMP is approved under CRZ 2019 — this decides 50 m vs 200 m. ☐ Measure from the demarcated HTL, not the waterline. ☐ Identify the clearance authority (central vs state) for that zone. ☐ Obtain a certified CZMP extract for the survey number. ☐ Engage a lawyer experienced in coastal regulation before money moves. Quick answers (FAQ) Minimum distance from the sea to build a house? Zone-dependent: 50 m in approved dense rural stretches, 200 m otherwise in rural coast, road-line rule in urban CRZ-II. Is the 50 m NDZ automatic? No — only after CZMP approval. Hotels and resorts? Possible in permitted stretches with clearance, never inside the NDZ or CRZ-I. Building without clearance? Fines, prosecution — and demolition orders that survive completion. Bottom line On the coast, the zone IS the value: the same acre is a resort site in CRZ-II, a 200-metre wait in IIIB, and a permanent no in CRZ-I. Verify zone, CZMP status and HTL for the exact survey number before believing any price.
